guidance: Q1 FY27 (September 2026 quarter): revenue $89.85-90.95B (+16-17%; midpoint $90.4B vs $89.66B LSEG consensus); Productivity & Business Processes $36.7-37.0B, Intelligent Cloud $40.95-41.25B, More Personal Computing $12.2-12.7B; Azure growth ~45% in constant currency (Visible Alpha consensus 40.92%), with H1 FY27 Azure growth expected to accelerate; operating margin roughly flat y/y; capex over $50B including the lease-reclassification impact (Visible Alpha consensus $56.02B); tax rate ~20%. Full FY27: double-digit revenue and operating income growth; operating margins down less than 1 point; capex to grow y/y. Calendar-2026 capex expectation now ~$175B vs ~$190B guided on 2026-04-29; company attributes the change to more datacenter leases being classified as operating leases (not included in capex) and says underlying CY2026 investment expectations are unchanged.
key_metrics: Azure and other cloud services revenue growth: +43% reported, +43% constant currency (company guidance given in April: 39-40% cc; Visible Alpha consensus 39.98%)

Capital expenditures: $41B including finance leases ($35.8B cash paid for PP&E; $5.6B finance leases) vs company guidance of 'over $40B' and Visible Alpha consensus $42.37B. Capex outlook given the same day: Q1 FY27 over $50B (Visible Alpha consensus $56.02B); FY27 capex to grow y/y; calendar-2026 capex ~$175B vs ~$190B prior, attributed to lease reclassification
other_announcements: Effective at the start of FY27, extending estimated useful lives of datacenters and office buildings from 15 to 25 years; company said this shifts more future datacenter leases from finance to operating leases (reducing reported capex) and has a minimal benefit to FY27 operating income
Returned $10.2B to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases in the quarter
headline: Microsoft FY26 Q4: revenue $90.0B vs $87.62B est; non-GAAP EPS $4.74 vs $4.24 est; Azure +43% vs 39-40% guide (39.98% est); capex $41B vs $42.37B est; guides Q1 FY27 revenue $89.85-90.95B vs $89.66B est, Azure ~45% cc vs 40.92% est, capex over $50B
notes: Revenue consensus differs slightly by provider ($87.61B-$87.72B); used $87.62B (FactSet as cited by AP, also cited as the LSEG figure). Company stated that discrete items versus its April guidance (including a $3.2B gain on its Anthropic investment and lower-than-expected Voluntary Retirement Program costs, partly offset by severance and Xbox impairment charges) added $0.27 to diluted EPS; these items are included in both GAAP and non-GAAP EPS.
